correctness.rationale: The positive radius h+h''=R−8ε cos(3θ) gives a unique analytic oval of width 2R. A zero of the support half-difference f=ε cos(3θ)−z·n must have f'=0 for a convex union, since two distinct singleton support points leave their joining segment uncovered. Analyticity and antipodality force a sign-changing zero; its multiplicity is then at least three. At that zero f''=−8ε cos(3θ), and f=f'=f''=0 yields exactly the three candidate vectors listed. For z=(−3ε,0), f=4ε cos³θ; at the only two switches the support points coincide. All boundary points of the hull are therefore covered, and the common point z (inside the disk of radius R−ε contained in K) gives coverage of the interior along rays. Rotation gives the other cases. The centered support is R+4ε|cos θ|³. At a join, the radius is R+24ε|θ−θ₀|+O(|θ−θ₀|³). Positive radius makes arclength a C¹ change of normal angle; the tangent is C¹ with respect to arclength, but curvature has unequal one-sided derivatives, proving C² and not C³ for the geometric boundary. The support integrals use ∫|cos θ|³=8/3, ∫cos⁶ θ=5π/8, and ∫9cos⁴ θ sin² θ=9π/8 over the full circle, giving the claimed perimeter and both areas. This is analytic throughout; the frozen sampling code was inspected as a diagnostic, not used as proof.
residual_risks: No claim at R=8ε or for ε=0, or for general support functions.

value.rationale: This is a sharpness example for a classic three-center lower bound in the restrictive class of analytic, strictly positively curved constant-width bodies. Unlike a cusp count alone it characterizes every reflection union that is convex, and the exact support, area gain and curvature joins give reusable information about those unions.
residual_risks: Only one harmonic family; no arbitrary-oval classification.
